name: HER_HAL_DUAL_HEAD_RULING

ruling.title: THE DUAL-HEAD RISK IS NOW THE HIGHEST-VALUE LOCAL QUESTION
ruling.correction: REPLAY was not missing. The unresolved question is whether HELEN has one authoritative committed-state root or two competing heads.

heads.note: Not automatically a defect — possibly intentional layered views. Until the relationship is established, the strongest capability invariant is under-specified.

ruling.target_invariant: kappa.h_pre = H(G_latest_committed), where 'latest committed' has exactly one machine-defined meaning — NOT kappa.h_pre = G_SM.

her_view.finding: Semantic ambiguity: 'current state' has two implementations. Both names sound authoritative while possibly representing different lifecycle moments.
her_view.hypothesis: G_SM = working/current application state; G_TX = durably committed governed state. If intentional, the distinction must be explicit in types and names; if not, semantic aliasing: same phrase != same state semantics.
her_view.instruction: Do not merge the heads until DH-01 tells us what relationship they actually have.

hal_view.single_question: Can a capability minted against one head successfully execute after the other head has advanced?
hal_view.law_candidate: InvokeSuccess(kappa) => kappa.h_pre = H(G_committed) at acceptance time.
hal_view.naming_law: Name(x) = StateManager does not imply x = authoritative committed root. This is C3 (non-transport) applied to subsystem naming.

dh01_falsifier.name: DH-01 DUAL-HEAD DIVERGENCE TEST
protocol: 5. observe exact state source used by Executor
dh01_falsifier.discriminator: Invoke(kappa) =? FAIL(E_STALE_STATE) — the committed world has already advanced.

classification.SAFE_DIVERGENCE: Executor uses latest committed root and rejects stale kappa.
classification.INTENTIONAL_LAYERING: Heads differ but contracts explicitly prevent misuse.
classification.DUAL_HEAD_FRACTURE: Executor accepts against stale non-committed head.

state_root_taxonomy.question: Which root does each module actually represent? Which head does Executor trust? Which head SHOULD Executor trust?
state_root_taxonomy.possible_resolution: StateManager = G_working, TransactionRuntime = G_committed. Then the bug is not 'two heads' — it is using the wrong head for capability validation. Smaller, cleaner repair than merging all state machinery.

boundary_patterns.state_changing: TYPE -> DERIVE -> BIND -> EXECUTE -> COMMIT -> REPLAY
boundary_patterns.note: WUL, HAL, and transactions instantiate different fibers of the same meta-pattern. WUL loss != HAL verification != TX closure.

repair_discipline.rule: Do not jump to UnifiedStore automatically. If DH-01 exposes a single wrong dependency, fix Executor -> committed_state_provider instead of building new storage abstraction.
repair_discipline.principle: Repair the violated boundary != redesign the world.
repair_discipline.unifiedstore_condition: Introduce only if evidence shows multiple duplicated authoritative roots requiring actual consolidation.

chiddush: HELEN's security depends less on how many witnesses it produces than on whether all privileged witnesses are anchored to the same committed world.
next_machine_question: G_SM != G_TX => which one does kappa actually trust? DH-01 answers this next.
frame_note: StateManager, TransactionRuntime and Executor are artifacts of another frame; on this filesystem E027 records the ruling and DH-01 as a PROPOSED falsifier design. Observed-there does not imply observed-here; the test earns its verdict only where those modules exist.
